text.p: These are the leading stories in Botswana's independent midweek newspapers, The Sun and The Gazette, on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- A media showdown looms as international media organisations join forces with local journalists to protest against the proposed Mass Media Communications Bill. The Bill echoes the 1960 Publications Bill in South Africa which sought to prohibit any publication labelled undesirable by the government, says Clive Emdone of the Freedom of Expression Institute of South Africa.
A delegation of journalists will meet minister responsible for the Press, Ponatshego Kedikilwe, on Wednesday.

- A confidential research report by the government has claimed that large-scale farmers are killing wildlife as they clear large areas of the wildnerness to make room for the expansion of their farms.

- The opening of Tswapong diamond mine has been delayed until objections to the mine's operations by members of the Bangwato tribe are sorted out. The tribe says it was not consulted about the mine and the possible relocation of some of its members.
